avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin C
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increases urinary uric acid excretion and may increase risk of urate crystal formation in kidneys; counteracts allopurinol efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin C intake to <2000 mg/day; monitor uric acid levels and renal function closely

avoid_supplements.name: Azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, reducing metabolism of these immunosuppressants, leading to severe toxicity and bone marrow suppression
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if required, reduce azathioprine/6-mercaptopurine dose by 65-75% and monitor CBC closely

caution_supplements.name: Febuxostat
caution_supplements.mechanism: Concurrent xanthine oxidase inhibitors may increase hypouricemic effect
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum uric acid levels; use together only under physician direction

caution_supplements.name: Iron supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Allopurinol may inhibit iron absorption slightly; iron may enhance oxidative stress
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2-3 hours; monitor for efficacy of both agents

avoid_foods.name: High-purine foods (organ meats, anchovies, sardines, mussels)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High dietary purine load increases uric acid production, potentially overwhelming allopurinol's effect and triggering gout flares
avoid_foods.action: Maintain low-purine diet; educate patient on purine content of foods

caution_foods.name: Alcohol (especially beer)
caution_foods.mechanism: Alcohol increases uric acid production and impairs renal excretion; beer contains high purines
caution_foods.action: Limit alcohol consumption; counsel patient to restrict to moderate intake or eliminate

caution_foods.name: High-fructose foods and beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Fructose metabolism increases uric acid production
caution_foods.action: Reduce intake of sugary drinks, honey, and high-fructose corn syrup

caution_foods.name: Caffeine
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly increase uric acid levels; minimal clinical significance
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake; excessive consumption should be avoided

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum uric acid levels, renal function (creatinine, eGFR), and liver function tests periodically, especially during initial therapy. Educate patients that allopurinol may precipitate acute gout flares early in treatment; concurrent colchicine or NSAIDs prophylaxis is typically recommended for 3-6 months.
